title: LLM's suck at making MMO's and in game markets.
author: Glittering_Focus1538
selftext:
So I made BoneScript, an open source declarative LLM friendly language that compiles system descriptions into complete, runnable Node.js backends.  
You can use it's Postgres, Nakama and other integrations to entirely write the backend of your game in hours instead of days.

comments.author: Glittering_Focus1538
comments.body:
# Why This Approach is Powerful for Games

* **Extremely fast iteration** — Change game rules in the .bone file → recompile → deploy.
* **Built-in correctness** — State machines, constraints, transactions, and preconditions are enforced automatically.
* **Real-time multiplayer** handled cleanly through channels.
* **Less boilerplate** — No manual writing of RPC handlers, database schemas, or WebSocket logic.
* **Deterministic & auditable** — The generated backend is predictable and maintainable.

In short: You write the **bones** (high-level design) of your game backend in BoneScript, and the compiler gives you the full **skeleton** — a complete Nakama backend ready to run.

replies.author: Glittering_Focus1538
replies.body:
BoneScript helps hobbyist game devs by letting you describe your game's backend in simple, high-level terms (like "players have inventory items with states, and a 'craft' action that checks resources then updates them"), then instantly generates a complete, runnable Node.js server with database, API endpoints, real-time WebSockets, auth, admin panel, and even Nakama support for multiplayer.

Instead of wiring up Express routes, SQL migrations, state machines, validation, events, and error handling manually, you focus on the game logic bones, constraints like "health > 0", state transitions like "alive → dead", or real-time channels for lobbies and the tool fills in the full professional skeleton deterministically every time.  
  
For a hobbyist or vibecoder, this means prototyping a full player progression system or item trading backend in minutes, testing it locally with the generated admin UI and TypeScript client, then iterating by tweaking the description and recompiling, without getting buried in boilerplate or backend complexity.

It turns vague ideas into working infrastructure fast, so you can stay in creative flow rather than debugging infrastructure. As for the comments about my profile pic, I simply don't care.
